newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Peacekeepers issue ultimatum to Liberia militia.
newsitem.headline: Peacekeepers issue ultimatum to Liberia militia.

text.p: The African peacekeeping force in Liberia said on Monday it may have to use force to evict rebels blocking food aid to parts of the war-ravaged country.
A statement by the ECOMOG force gave guerrillas of General Roosevelt Johnson's ULIMO-J militia until Wednesday to clear roadblocks from the Tubmanburg and Cape Mount highways.
"ECOMOG wishes to state clearly that it would not hesitate to use force to ensure the safety of the highways," said a statement by ECOMOG commander General Victor Malu.

The Nigerian-led ECOMOG and ULIMO-J fought intense battles in the area last December and January. The violence led on to an explosion of militia warfare in Monrovia in April that derailed a peace accord on ending Liberia's six-year-old civil war.
West African leaders trying to end the civil war that has killed more than 150,000 people managed to pressure warlords last month to agree a new accord setting elections for May.
The accord and disarmament appeared to be generally on course until clashes erupted in western Liberia last month with ULIMO-J again at the centre of the violence.

General Malu said his 8,000-strong force was awaiting additional troops from six West African countries to begin a nation-wide deployment in readiness to disarm some 60,000 guerrillas under the accord.
